newsitem.title: USA: Inco Homes seeks to amend defaulted loans.
newsitem.headline: Inco Homes seeks to amend defaulted loans.

text.p: Inco Homes Corp said Tuesday it was in talks with a commercial bank that filed notices of default in January related to matured loans with principal balances totaling $3.5 million.
Inco said it was seeking to amend the terms of the loans, but it said there could be no assurances the bank would not sell the property securing the loans.
The loans are secured by an estimated 1,140 lots and 71 commercially zoned acres in Southern California, it said.
The law permits the bank to proceed with a non-judicial sale of the property as of April 9, or 90 days after the notices of default were filed, the company said.
The final settlement could result in writedowns in 1997 ranging from minimal to $6 million, Inco said.

The home builder said it was continuing its efforts to raise additional funds for working capital and the acquisition of land for future projects in Southern California. If it is not successful, some or all of its projects will be significantly delayed or abandoned, it said.
The company said it was unable to predict if it would be successful in raising capital, or if the terms of any capital raised would be favorable.
Inco said it has experienced and expects to continue to experience significant variability in its operating results.
